title: Cleanout Accessibility and Maintenance
description: Cleanouts are vital access points in any drainage system, allowing technicians to clear obstructions and inspect pipes without cutting into walls or disassembling traps. A common installation oversight is placing cleanouts in inaccessible locations, such as behind finished walls or beneath permanent fixtures. Professional best practice is to install cleanouts at major changes of direction, at the base of stacks, and on long horizontal runs. Always ensure adequate clearance in front of the cleanout plug to allow a drain auger or sewer camera to enter smoothly. Keeping cleanouts accessible saves significant time and prevents costly structural damage during future service.
